articles.title: Storm Rachel batters California, brings flooding to Las Vegas
articles.summary: Large waves from the post-tropical cyclone battered homes in Long Beach, and brought flooding to parts of Las Vegas near the famed Strip.
articles.body:

articles.title: Just how big is India’s 2024 election? Find out in seven numbers
articles.summary: About 969 million people will take part in the giant elections to decide who will rule the world’s most populous nation.
articles.body:
New Delhi, India – India, the world’s largest democracy, has kicked off its two and a half month long parliamentary election to decide who will rule the South Asian nation.

On Saturday, the Election Commission of India – the country’s independent poll-conducting body – announced the dates for a democratic exercise that is unmatched in scale globally, and in history.

From the Himalayas in the north to the Indian Ocean in the south, from the hills of the east to the deserts in the west, and in concrete jungles that are some of the world’s biggest cities to the smallest of villages, an estimated 969 million voters are eligible to cast their ballots. They will elect 543 politicians to the Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament. Two other members are nominated, to make up a total strength of 545 in the house.

India’s election is colossal, colourful and complex. Here are seven ways in which it is unparalleled in size.

The election process that started on Saturday will continue for 82 days until results are announced on June 4. With the announcement of the schedule, a model code of conduct also kicks in – campaign rules now apply, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government is not supposed to announce new policies that could influence voters.

Voting will run in seven phases from April 19 to June 1, said Rajiv Kumar, chief election commissioner of India. The counting of votes will take place on June 4. Assembly elections for the states of Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Odisha and Sikkim will also take place along with the national elections.

After April 19, the other voting dates are April 26, May 7, May 13, May 20, May 25 and June 1. Some states will complete voting on a single day, while others will have voting spread out across several phases.

Over the years, the number of days over which voting has stretched has varied a lot – from the shortest ever four days in 1980 to 39 days in the 2019 election, to 44 days in 2024.

The primary reason for the multiphased election is for the deployment of huge federal security forces required to check everything from polling-related violence or attempts at rigging, according to N Gopalaswami, the former chief election commissioner of India.

Still, staggered polls are no guarantee for free and fair elections as longer campaigning favours the ruling party of the day, said N Bhaskara Rao, chairman of the New Delhi-based Centre for Media Studies, and a pioneer in election research in India. Rao argued that the process should be shortened. The longer the process, the more the opportunity for the ruling party to use government infrastructure to campaign.

The size of India’s electorate is more than the population of all the countries of Europe combined.

They will cast their votes through 5.5 million electronic voting machines at 1.05 million polling stations, of which some are located in the snow-clad mountains in the Himalayas, the deserts of Rajasthan and sparsely populated islands in the Indian Ocean.

The Election Commission will deploy about 15 million polling staff and security personnel to conduct the elections. They will trek across glaciers and deserts, ride elephants and camels, and travel by boats and helicopters to ensure every voter can cast their ballot.

It is expected to be the world’s most expensive election. Spending by political parties and candidates to woo voters will likely cost more than 1.2 trillion rupees ($14.4bn), said Rao, whose organisation regularly estimates the country’s poll expenditure.

That would be twice what was spent in India’s 2019 elections – 600 billion rupees ($7.2bn). The total spending on the US presidential and congressional races in 2020 was also $14.4bn.

Most of India’s election spending is not publicly disclosed. Candidates spend unaccounted money to woo voters. The election scrutiny machinery is weak in detecting cash transactions, said Gopalaswami, referring to attempts by candidates to directly bribe voters with money or other enticements, from alcohol to clothes.

Holding elections in the world’s seventh largest nation by area is a complex task.

In 2019, election workers travelled 300 miles (482 km) over four days across winding mountain roads and river valleys to set up a polling booth for one voter in the northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh, which borders China. Beijing claims a part of the state, and ensuring elections are held there is vital for New Delhi to demonstrate its sovereignty over the region.

Election officials also set up a voting booth at 15,256 feet (4,650 metres) in a village in the northern state of Himachal Pradesh, making it the highest polling station in the world. Far off the country’s east coast, on the remote Andaman and Nicobar Islands, workers travelled through crocodile-infested mangrove swamps and dense jungles to reach polling booths.

In Malkangiri district of Odisha, where left-wing Maoist fighters have a presence, polling staff walked 15km (9 miles) through forests and hills to protect electronic voting machines from the rebels after voting. Intelligence agencies had warned them that using cars could have made them easier targets.

“On sheer numbers, it’s gigantic and complicated, but in a sense simple also because at each level the law is very clear about what are the duties and responsibilities of each polling official,’’ said Gopalaswmi. “Complications are arising as competition is becoming fierce,’’ he said, adding, that implementation of the model code of conduct has become increasingly challenging for the election commission.

A multiparty democracy, India has about 2,660 registered political parties. Parties competing in elections each get symbols – like the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s lotus, the opposition Congress party’s hand, and others, ranging from an elephant to a bicycle, and a comb to an arrow. These to help voters easily identify candidates, in a country where almost a quarter of the population is not literate.

In 2019, seven national parties, 43 state parties and 623 unrecognised political parties participated in the elections. Parties that have a significant footprint in a state legislature are recognised as state parties. Those with a meaningful presence in multiple states get the national party tag.

In 2019, 36 parties were able to win one or more seats in the Lok Sabha. In all, about 8,054 candidates, including 3,461 independents, contested those elections. Of the 543 winning candidates, 397 were from national parties, 136 were from state parties, six were from unrecognised parties and four were independent.

A record 612 million people of a 912 million strong electorate cast their votes in the last election, registering the highest ever voter turnout at 67.4 percent. Women’s participation also increased to an historic 67.18 percent in 2019.

The principal protagonists of the 2024 battle are Prime Minister Modi and his BJP, who lead a coalition of more than three dozen parties; and the main opposition Congress party-led alliance of about two dozen parties.

In 2019, the BJP secured a landslide victory with 303 seats. Its coalition had a total of 353 seats. The Congress party won got 52 seats, and 91 with partners.

Currently, the BJP is in pole position following recent state victories and is expected to win a majority, according to opinion polls. The BJP alone controls 12 of India’s 28 states, while the Congress governs in three states.

Still, Indian political history is littered with instances of parties winning major state elections only to lose the national vote soon after. The BJP knows that better than most: In 2004, its then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee called early elections after winning the key state elections of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh before losing the Lok Sabha vote to a Congress-led coalition.

Modi has set a target of 370 seats for the BJP, 67 more than in 2019; and for its alliance to cross 400 seats. He is seeking a third term in office.

The last time any party crossed 370 seats was in the 1984 election. The Congress party won 414 seats following the assassination of the former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

If Modi wins and completes five years, he will be the third longest serving prime minister in Indian history. The country’s first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru ruled for about 16 years and 9 months consecutively, while his daughter Indira Gandhi governed for a total of about 15 years and 11 months.

articles.title: The expert-approved methods (and products) for cleaning coats and jackets without ruining them
articles.summary: I found the best cleaning products and methods for cleaning jackets and coats after talking with laundry and dry cleaning experts.
articles.body: When fall rolls around and the weather starts cooling off, you know it’s time to either stock up on new winter apparel or refresh what you already have. Knowing the best way to clean your coats and jackets is especially important since some of them have been sitting in your closet for months. The only problem is that sometimes it’s not as simple as throwing something into the washing machine or dusting it off. With that in mind, I reached out to laundry experts to learn how to properly clean coats and jackets without ruining them or jeopardizing the look and feel of their material. Below, I explain the methods they recommend for cleaning your winter garments. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for cleaning coats and jackets All of the products below are either direct recommendations from our experts or editors and/or have at least a 4-star average rating from 500 or more customers on Amazon. Best laundry detergent tablet As a home and kitchen editor, Blueland is one of my favorite cleaning brands and one I recommend all the time. These enzyme-based detergent tablets are completely plastic free, so there’s no film or pouch. I love that they easily dissolve in cold water, which is perfect for washing sensitive clothing like jackets, since experts recommend only using cold water. This bag comes with 60 tablets, which are around the size of a regular dishwasher tablet, and are available in both scented and unscented options. Best for wool coats This clothes brush is made with bristles from fine-textured boar hair and it’s great for cleaning debris from wool coats, upholstery, cashmere and more, according to the brand. If you have a wool coat that you don’t have time to take to the dry cleaner, you can try to give it a light clean with this brush. One shopper who has several wool coats in their home says it’s easy to use, even on lint, and it’s so durable that it’s something “anyone with wool coats should have.” Best spray This fabric spray not only gets rid of bacteria trapped in clothing, but it also helps get rid of odors, according to Tide. It leaves your coats and other garments sanitized and smelling fresh, without having to throw them in the washing machine. Aside from clothing, you can use it on bedding, towels and more. One shopper even says they enjoy using this particularly for things like jackets and other sensitive items that shouldn’t be washed often. Best laundry sanitizer Lysol’s Free & Clear laundry sanitizing detergent is ideal for those who want to throw their coats and jackets in the wash but only with a gentle option that won’t ruin the texture. Since it’s a sanitizer, it gets rid of bacteria on coats and jackets while also refreshing them. It’s free of fragrances, dyes and bleach, and it’s suitable for cold water, which is best for washing coats and jackets, according to experts. Best laundry detergent sheet If you prefer to use a more sustainable option, these popular laundry detergent sheets from Earth Breeze can help clean and refresh your coats without any parabens, dyes or preservatives. The hypoallergenic sheets dissolve in the wash with your clothes, even in cold water. The sheets are plastic free and the box is 100 percent recyclable (contributing to its sustainability). They help get rid of stains and odors while also preventing coats from fading, according to the brand. Best laundry detergent powder Laundry boosters give your detergent extra help when it comes to clearing stains and odors from your coats and jackets. This free and clear powder helps maintain the vibrancy of your garments and removes yellow stains from sweat. It’s free of surfactants, dyes and fragrances, and works in cold water, according to the brand. Best for odors Downy’s Rinse Out Odor helps get rid of odors and stains more thoroughly while working with your detergent. It can replace fabric softener and works with your detergent to help clean your coats and other garments. This free and clear option has no fragrances and dyes and is also safe for sensitive skin, according to the brand. You can use it on all fabric types and is also safe to use on activewear, towels and more. How to clean coats and jackets Before simply adding your coat to a washer, it’s best to consider the care instructions on the label, according to Frej Lewenhaupt, co-founder and chief product officer of Steamery, a clothing care company. “Since winter jackets vary in size and material, I recommend checking the care label to see if it can be washed and dried with your machine,” he says. “Many modern washing machines have wool or delicate cycles that are gentle enough, but you still want to use cold water and a mild detergent.” If the label says it’s safe to clean in a washing machine, then the most important thing is to avoid heat, including both water and dryer heat, according to Lewenhaupt. This is because “it can cause shrinkage and degrade the waterproof coating. If you’re unsure, it’s best to handwash and lay the jacket flat to dry,” he says. With that said, different materials require various methods for cleaning and some should not be washed in a machine or by hand, but instead brought to a professional dry cleaner. Here are some tips on how to maintain coats of different types: How to clean a wool coat In general, it’s best to get your wool coats dry cleaned since putting them in the washer and dryer can change and damage their texture, appearance and shape. Many high-quality wool coats, from brands like Quince, Mango, Nordstrom and J.Crew have labels saying to dry clean only. If you do have a wool or wool blend jacket or garment that says that it is machine washable, and you don’t want to bring it to the dry cleaner, then you should still wash with caution to prevent damage. In this case, it’s best to use a mild detergent (often labeled “free & clear”), cold water and the lowest heat setting for drying, according to Lewenhaupt. Additionally, some machines have a setting for wool or sensitive fabrics, which Lewenhaupt recommends using for a wool coat.It’s also important to know that wool has natural antibacterial properties, according to textile experts I’ve spoken to in the past. So wool coats don’t really have to be cleaned that often, unless they are especially smelly or soiled. Otherwise, you can use a boar-bristle brush, such as the BFWood Boar Bristle Clothes Brush, to maintain them. How to clean down and fleece coats To clean your down or fleece coat by hand, use a fabric freshener, such as Tide Antibacterial Fabric Spray, which kills bacteria but also gets rid of odors. Lewenhaupt also recommends using a spray in between washes since washing too often can alter the texture of fleece (and wool), and it can deteriorate the feathers of a down jacket and cause it to lose its loft and insulation. If the care instructions for your down or fleece coat say it’s safe to throw in the washing machine (and you haven’t machine washed it for at least a few months), then put it in the machine with cold water and use a fabric-gentle detergent like Lysol Free & Clear Laundry Sanitizer. If the jacket is especially dirty or smelly, use a laundry booster like Downy Free & Gentle Laundry Odor Remover Rinse. How to clean denim jackets To clean denim jackets, Lewenhaupt recommends either hand washing them or machine washing them on a gentle cycle, since denim is prone to fading. “Turning your jacket inside out before washing is a great way to protect the outer surface and preserve the color,” he says. “I recommend using a mild, color-safe detergent and to check for and pre-treat stains before washing to make the removal process easier.” Lewnehaupt also recommends air drying your denim jacket as opposed to machine drying it to prevent shrinking.” As a natural fabric, denim benefits from being aired out and can be quickly refreshed with a steamer to go longer between washes,” he says. How to clean leather and suede coats Due to the sensitive nature of leather and suede, Lewnehaupt recommends never putting coats and jackets made from these fabrics in a washer or dryer to avoid ruining the materials. Instead, “a damp cloth is usually enough to wipe away light dirt and then you can use a leather conditioner to keep the material from drying out or cracking,” he says. “When cleaning suede, use a soft suede brush to lift away dirt and spot-treat any stains with a suede cleaner and avoid applying water directly.” You can also use a specialized leather or suede cleaner. Meet our experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. We did not ask Romine for product recommendations, though Procter & Gamble does benefit if any of its products are purchased from this story. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected where I write about cleaning, appliances, organization and more. I’ve written about different fabric types, how to clean a mattress and how to clean stuffed animals and plush toys. For this story, I spoke with cleaning experts for their product recommendations and guidance on how to clean different types of coats and jackets. articles.title: Elon Musk gastou US$ 366 milhões em doações para republicanos | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresário gastou, desde fevereiro, cerca de US$ 366 milhões nas eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 para ajudar republicanos a manter o controle do Congresso.
articles.summary: Elon Musk destinou US$ 366 milhões a grupos republicanos e super PACs para influenciar as eleições de 2026 e proteger seus contratos com o governo.
articles.body:
O empresário Elon Musk gastou cerca de US$ 366 milhões (R$ 1,8 bilhão) para apoiar o Partido Republicano, do presidente Donald Trump , no ciclo eleitoral das eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 nos Estados Unidos.

Desse total, US$ 276 milhões (R$ 1,3 bilhão) foram doados desde julho. A informação foi divulgada inicialmente pelo jornal "The New York Times".

Com isso, Musk se torna o maior o doador individual nas eleições deste ano, de acordo com os registros de financiamento de campanha. Esta é uma mudança drástica no posicionamento político do empresário. Em maio do ano passado, Musk disse que pretendia reduzir seus gastos políticos. “Acho que já fiz o suficiente”, disse ele na época.

➡️ As eleições de meio de mandato, conhecidas como midterms , acontecem nos Estados Unidos a cada quatro anos, na metade do mandato presidencial. Neste ano, acontecem no dia 3 de novembro. Nelas, os americanos renovam a Câmara dos Representantes e cerca de um terço do Senado, definindo o controle do Congresso. Hoje o Partido Republicano tem maioria nas duas Casas.

➡️ Musk é dono de empresas como a SpaceX e a Tesla. Recentemente, a sua fortuna voltou a ser estimada em mais de US$ 1 trilhão, segundo a Fortune.

Elon Musk , CEO da Tesla e da SpaceX e proprietário do X, anteriormente conhecido como Twitter, discursa durante o evento de lançamento do America.gov, um novo site governamental com inteligência artificial, organizado pelo National Design Studio, no Mellon Auditorium em Washington, DC, EUA, em 29 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

A iniciativa de Musk é interpretada por veículos da imprensa internacional como uma ofensiva contra democratas do Congresso americano, que pedem investigações sobre seus contratos com o governo como CEO da empresa aeroespacial SpaceX. Também há pedidos sobre sua atuação à frente do Departamento de Eficiência Governamental no governo Trump.

Musk teve um desentendimento com Trump ao deixar seu cargo no governo, mas os dois se reconciliaram. Trump concedeu a Musk a Medalha Nacional de Ciência na semana passada. O empresário também voltou ao governo, agora como conselheiro de um estudo sobre o futuro da guerra.

O montante doado inclui US$ 158 milhões doados ao Fundo de Liderança do Senado, o principal fundo que apoia candidatos republicanos . Outros US$ 76 milhões foram destinados ao "America PAC" — Comitê de Ação Política de Musk—, criado para arrecadar fundos para campanhas eleitorais.

Musk também doou US$ 10 milhões para o Lone Star Liberty PAC, um grupo que apoia o candidato republicano ao Senado pelo Texas, Ken Paxton.

Veja o detalhamento dos gastos políticos de Musk , segundo a agência de notícias Reuters:

Musk gastou US$ 366 milhões neste ciclo eleitoral, iniciado em 1º de janeiro de 2025;

Deste total, doou pelo menos US$ 276 milhões a grupos republicanos e ao seu próprio comitê de ação polícia, o America PAC, no terceiro trimestre, a partir de julho.

As doações do terceiro trimestre foram distribuídas da seguinte forma:

US$ 158 milhões foram ao Fundo de Liderança do Senado (Senate Leadership Fund), comitê de ação política criado para ajudar a eleger republicanos para o Senado e alinhado ao líder da maioria na Casa, John Thune, da Dakota do Sul.

US$ 20 milhões foram ao Congressional Leadership Fund, comitê que apoia republicanos na Câmara dos Representantes e é alinhado ao presidente da Casa, Mike Johnson, da Louisiana.

Mais US$ 76 milhões foram enviados ao America PAC, de Musk.

US$ 10 milhões foram ao Lone Star Liberty PAC, que apoia a candidatura do procurador-geral republicano Ken Paxton ao Senado dos Estados Unidos pelo Texas. Pesquisas recentes mostram Paxton em empate técnico com o democrata James Talarico.

articles.standfirst: A causa da morte não foi divulgada. Ele ficou conhecido ao interpretar o filho do protagonista, vivido por Bryan Cranston, na série premiada.
articles.summary: A causa da morte não foi divulgada. Ele ficou conhecido ao interpretar o filho do protagonista, vivido por Bryan Cranston, na série premiada.
articles.body:
RJ Mitte, que interpretou Walter White Jr. em 'Breaking Bad' — Foto: Divulgação/AMC

O ator RJ Mitte, que ficou conhecido por interpretar Walter White Jr. na série "Breaking Bad" , morreu na segunda-feira (11) nos Estados Unidos, aos 34 anos.

Cyndi Hinojosa, autoridade judicial do condado de Cameron, disse à Associated Press que declarou a morte de Mitte por volta das 13h30 em uma residência que seria a casa do ator, em Brownsville, no Texas. A causa da morte não foi divulgada, mas o corpo do ator passará por autópsia.

Na série, Mitte interpretou o filho do protagonista Walter White, interpretado por Bryan Cranston. A série, exibida entre 2008 e 2013, conta a história de um professor de química que passa a produzir metanfetamina para enriquecer. A produção recebeu prêmios como Emmy e Globo de Ouro e, recentemente, foi eleita a melhor série do século XXI pelo jornal "The New York Times".

Mitte convivia com paralisia cerebral e atuava também como ativista da causa de pessoas com deficiência. "Com base em sua própria experiência de vida com paralisia cerebral, Mitte trouxe autenticidade ao papel [em 'Breaking Bad'] e construiu uma plataforma de conscientização e inclusão das pessoas com deficiência", disse, em comunicado divulgado pela Variety, um representante do ator.

Segundo o TMZ, a causa da morte está sendo investigada pela polícia.

Além de "Breaking Bad", o ator atuou também em produções como "Triumph" e "Westhampton".

Mitte ficou noivo de sua namorada de longa data, Kennedy Suarez, no ano passado. O anúncio foi feito em reportagem na revista People.

articles.standfirst: Evento teve 8 horas de duração e ocorreu no Anfiteatro da Represa de São José do Rio Preto (SP).
articles.summary: Parada da Diversidade em Rio Preto celebrou a resistência LGBTQIAPN+ com oito horas de shows, performances de drag queens e apresentação da Pocah.
articles.body:
A Parada da Diversidade reuniu cerca de 20 mil pessoas no Anfiteatro da Represa Municipal de São José do Rio Preto (SP) no domingo (11).

Com oito horas de duração, o evento teve a participação em peso da comunidade LGBTQIAPN+, apresentações de drag queens, a presença de Miss trans e o show da cantora Pocah .

Parada da Diversidade reúne multidão em São José do Rio Preto — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

Em entrevista à TV TEM , a drag queen Artemis Latte destacou a importância de ter um espaço seguro que garanta a liberdade de expressão.

"Muitas vezes não podemos ser quem somos dentro da nossa própria casa. Então, quando surge qualquer oportunidade de conseguir ser nós mesmos, fora e dentro de casa também, porque nossos pais começam a entender esse acolhimento de fora, levar isso para dentro de casa é muito lindo e gratificante. Tudo o que a gente faz é em forma de arte", ressaltou Artemis.

Artemis Latte, drag queen, participa da oitava parada da diversidade em São José do Rio Preto — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

A arte também esteve presente nos figurinos do público e nos shows da programação. A drag queen rio-pretense Margo Killer, que há 28 anos se apresenta pelo país, destacou o respeito às mulheres em sua performance.

“A minha drag queen, em particular, faz homenagem às mulheres. Como nasci homem, me torno uma mulher para homenagear as mulheres. Porque a mulher é guerreira, inspiração, força, coragem e resistência”, explicou Margo.

Drag Queen há 28 anos, Margo Killer marcou presença na Parada da Diversidade de São José do Rio Preto — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

Moradores de cidades vizinhas, como Catanduva e Mirassol (SP), marcaram presença no encontro que buscou reforçar a luta por direitos, como explicou Samuel Miranda, o organizador do evento.

“Essa festa é um momento de resistência. Estamos num marco da nossa cidade para falar que existimos, resistimos e somos muito mais do que simplesmente uma brincadeira do cotidiano. Nós somos força”, afirmou Samuel.

Oitava Parada da Diversidade reúne multidão em São José do Rio Preto — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

A criadora da primeira edição do evento, Abigail Rosseline, celebrou a consolidação do movimento em São José do Rio Preto.

“Fico feliz que o manifesto continue ativo, porque é uma luta que deu muito trabalho para a gente levantar e, hoje, faz parte do calendário anual da cidade. É uma conquista para todos nós”, concluiu.

Abigail Rosseline criadora da primeira Parada Gay de São José do Rio Preto — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

Conforme os organizadores, no horário de maior fluxo, entre 18h e 22h, cerca de 15 a 20 mil pessoas participaram do evento.

articles.title: Cadu defende obras viárias para integrar regiões e ampliar turismo | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT prometeu construir terceira ponte sobre o rio Potengi, em Natal, a nova estrada de Pipa, em Tibau do Sul, e implantar a BR Litorânea, entre Areia Branca e Macau.
articles.summary: Candidato do PT prometeu construir terceira ponte sobre o rio Potengi, em Natal, a nova estrada de Pipa, em Tibau do Sul, e implantar a BR Litorânea, entre Areia Branca e Macau.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte pelo PT, Cadu de Lula, realizou nesta segunda-feira (12) uma carreata na Zona Norte de Natal , com concentração na Praia da Redinha. O candidato esteve acompanhado da senadora eleita Samanda Alves (PT), e de vereadores e deputados que apoiam a sua candidatura.

Cadu de Lula defende obras viárias para integrar regiões e ampliar turismo no RN — Foto: Luiz Thé/Inter TV Cabugi

Apoiadores de Cadu se concentraram próximo à Ponte Newton Navarro para o início da mobilização. Em seguida, os participantes acompanharam o candidato em carreata por vias da região. Ao longo do trajeto, Cadu conversou com moradores e recebeu relatos sobre o dia a dia e o trânsito no local. A pauta da mobilidade urbana e da ligação viária da capital esteve no centro dos diálogos mantidos durante o percurso com quem acompanhava a passagem dos carros.

"Esse projeto da terceira ponte é um sonho da população da Zona Norte de Natal, principalmente. A gente sabe que é uma obra milionária, a gente tem que ter muita responsabilidade. É uma obra importante para a mobilidade, para conectar cada vez mais a cidade, para a cidade se integrar. E eu tenho certeza que, ao lado do presidente Lula, nós vamos realizar esse sonho que é fazer a terceira ponte", comentou.

Cadu também defendeu investimentos em segurança e uma nova estrada em direção à Praia da Pipa, para incentivar o fluxo turístico no litoral Sul do RN. Outro projeto defendido pelo candidato é a chamada BR Litorânea, que, para ele, é um passo importante para conectar todas as regiões do estado.

"O turismo tem que ter um olhar especial pelo governo do estado. A gente tem que investir em segurança, infraestrutura, conexão, para que pessoas de todo o mundo possam vir aqui para o Rio Grande do Norte. É esse o trabalho que a gente vai fazer, promover cada vez mais o nosso estado, dar segurança para os destinos turísticos do nosso estado. A nova estrada de Pipa é uma proposta nossa, que nós vamos realizar e também a BR Litorânea, que liga Areia Branca a Macau, para a gente levar o turismo para todas as regiões do estado", concluiu Cadu.

articles.title: Incêndio em Teresina: fogo atinge depósito de reciclagem no São Pedro | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradores da região foram orientados a retirar pertences e animais de suas residências por segurança.
articles.summary: O incêndio em Teresina no bairro São Pedro levou moradores a evacuarem casas após suspeita de que fogos de artifício atingiram o depósito de reciclagem.
articles.body:
Depósito de reciclagem pega fogo em Teresina; bombeiros apontam suspeita de fogos de artifício — Foto: Reprodução

Um depósito de reciclagem pegou fogo na tarde desta segunda-feira (12) no Bairro São Pedro, Zona Sul de Teresina. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a equipe foi acionada por moradores da região após o surgimento de focos de incêndio no local. Conforme relatos repassados aos bombeiros, a suspeita inicial é que fogos de artifício tenham provocado as chamas .

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, além do depósito de reciclagem, ao menos duas casas também foram atingidas pelo incêndio. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Ainda de acordo com os bombeiros, vizinhos relataram que houve uma queima de fogos de artifício nas proximidades horas antes do incêndio. A suspeita inicial é que faíscas tenham atingido materiais armazenados no depósito e provocado as chamas.

O imóvel fica próximo a casas geminadas. Por segurança, os moradores foram orientados a retirar pertences e animais das residências e permanecer afastados da área atingida.

O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) também foi acionado para atender moradores que passaram mal por causa da fumaça provocada pelo incêndio.

Ao menos cinco viaturas do Corpo de Bombeiros foram mobilizadas para controlar as chamas no depósito de reciclagem.

Durante o combate ao incêndio, uma das viaturas precisou retornar à base para reabastecimento de água. Segundo a corporação, a equipe voltou ao local e deu continuidade aos trabalhos.

articles.title: In 1981, Francis Ford Coppola found an abandoned Belize jungle lodge and turned it into a family retreat; 12 years later Blancaneaux opened as a 20-room resort, now drawing about 85% of its power from a creek
articles.summary: In 1981, American filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola bought an abandoned hunting lodge in the forests of western Belize.
articles.body: In 1981, American filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola bought an abandoned hunting lodge in the forests of western Belize. The private retreat for his family later became Blancaneaux Lodge, a 20-room resort surrounded by pine forests, rivers and waterfalls. The property, which the Coppola family used for years before opening it to visitors, continues to retain much of its original character.Located in a forested area of Belize, Blancaneaux Lodge was initially a place where Coppola and his family could spend time away from their regular lives. His children grew up visiting the property, swimming in the river and exploring the surrounding forests. Over time, the family's connection with the location became an important part of the resort's identity.According to Conde Nast Traveler, the lodge eventually opened to guests in 1993, around 12 years after Coppola purchased the property and continues to attract visitors interested in outdoor activities and a quiet stay in the forest.Coppola's daughter, filmmaker Sofia Coppola, recalled spending her childhood holidays at the lodge with her brothers. “I'd hop around on rocks and swim in the river with my brothers,” she told Conde Nast Traveler. “I feel so lucky to have had these jungle adventures.”Abandoned hunting lodge to family retreatWhen Francis Ford Coppola acquired the property in 1981, it was a disused hunting lodge. He converted it into a private retreat where his family could spend time together in the forests of Belize.The surrounding landscape became an important part of their visits. The property is located near a creek, with forests and waterfalls in the surrounding area. The family spent time exploring these places, and the lodge gradually became a familiar holiday destination for Coppola's children.Years later, the family decided to open the property to visitors. Blancaneaux Lodge became a 20-room resort, offering accommodation in cottages designed to retain the character of the original retreat.Although access routes have improved since the family's early visits, the property has undergone relatively few changes in appearance. Its cottages remain naturally cooled by the breeze, while the wood-panelled Jaguar Bar displays photographs of earlier archaeological excavations.Sofia Coppola said the lodge's familiar appearance remains one of the things she appreciates about it. “I love that Blancaneaux has felt the same over the years which is rustic but comfortable,” she said.The Blancaneaux LodgeThe resort's location allows guests to explore the surrounding landscape through several outdoor activities. Visitors can go kayaking through cave systems, where passages run between formations of stalactites. Horse riding is another activity, with routes leading to waterfalls where guests can swim.The lodge's surroundings also provide opportunities to experience the forests and waterways of western Belize.While the property has developed into a resort, its accommodation and shared spaces continue to reflect the family's preference for relatively simple surroundings. The cottages, wooden interiors and outdoor setting remain important features of Blancaneaux.Sofia Coppola's resort connectionThe family's involvement with Blancaneaux has continued into the next generation. Sofia Coppola, who spent time there as a child, has also worked on a collaboration connected with the property's spa.In 2024, she collaborated with Monastery, a San Francisco-based botanical skincare company founded by aesthetician Athena Hewett.Hewett had previously sent Sofia a bottle of cleansing oil from her skincare range. Sofia later visited Monastery's spa for a treatment, and the two began discussing a product that could be used at Blancaneaux. “Sofia loved that we were plant-based and small-batch,” Hewett said.Their collaboration resulted in a facial mist containing rosewood from Central America, rose and orchid oil. The product was developed for treatments at the Blancaneaux spa and as something visitors could take home.Blancaneaux is not the family's only hospitality property in Belize. The Coppolas also own Turtle Inn, a coastal retreat near the Belize Barrier Reef system.Unlike the forest setting of Blancaneaux, Turtle Inn offers access to marine activities. The property has thatched cabanas, carved wooden doors, Japanese soaking tubs and pathways lined with hibiscus.Sofia also has a bungalow at Turtle Inn, where she spends time with her husband, musician Thomas Mars, and their daughters. She wrote the screenplay for Priscilla while staying there.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: In 1996, Bill Clinton created Grand Staircase-Escalante with 1.7 million federal acres; decades of boundary fights later reshaped the Utah monument
articles.summary: In 1996, President Bill Clinton designated the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in Utah, protecting 1.7 million acres of unique geological features and archaeological sites, amid debates on conservation versus mineral development. This article explores the monument's history, boundary changes, and the ongoing significance of this landscape.
articles.body: In September 1996, President Bill Clinton protected about 1.7 million acres of federal lands that have geologic features, dinosaur fossils, archaeological sites, and wildlife habitats in order to create the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in southern Utah. This move was made during a debate on the future of the region. President Clinton designated the national monument through the Antiquities Act of 1906 on September 18, entrusting the management of the site to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) of the Department of the Interior. Initially, the designation covered about 1.7 million acres, but it was expanded by Congress to cover about 1.87 million acres.Why Utah’s canyon country is important conflict groundThe region contains a broad range of landscapes, including the Grand Staircase’s layered rock formations, the Escalante Canyons and the Kaiparowits Plateau. The area’s geological record, fossil deposits and archaeological remains make it important for scientific research. Bill Clinton’s original proclamation identified these resources among the reasons for protecting the area. Additionally, the landscape preserves evidence of past human activity, including archaeological sites associated with Indigenous communities.The debate was also related to mineral development, since there are large coal resources at the Kaiparowits Plateau. It involved a potential coal mining project. The Clinton administration’s stated aim included preventing development of significant coal reserves and protecting the region’s historic and scientific resources. Supporters of mining argued that development could provide economic benefits. However, conservationists were concerned with the outcomes for the landscape and its resources. The Los Angeles Times reported opposition from the Utah government to the designation, indicating that it was controversial.How Clinton set aside 1.7 million acresThe then-president announced the designation on September 18, 1996, from the South Rim of the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Proclamation 6920 invoked the Antiquities Act, which explicitly authorises presidents to designate national monuments on federal lands to protect objects of historic or scientific significance. This proclamation reserved approximately 1.7 million acres of federal land in Utah and assigned management responsibility to the BLM. Furthermore, it directed the Interior Secretary to prepare a management plan. This designation was subject to valid existing rights, and the proclamation particularly provided that existing livestock-grazing permits and uses would continue under applicable laws and regulations.From expansion to repeated boundary changesThe monument’s boundaries did not remain fixed after 1996. On three occasions, Congress made adjustments, including through legislation in 1998 and 2009, increasing the federal acreage reserved within the monument by 170,000 acres. Consequently, the total area reached 1.87 million acres. In December 2017, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation removing around 861,974 acres from the monument. Conservation organisations and paleontologists challenged the removal, arguing that while the Antiquities Act allows presidents to establish monuments, it does not grant them the reciprocal authority to reduce or dissolve them.President Joe Biden then restored the monument to 1.87 million acres, its immediate size before the removal in 2017, through a proclamation in October 2021. Nevertheless, the issue regarding its boundary did not stop there. More recently, on July 13, 2026, President Donald Trump issued another proclamation reducing the monument to approximately 181,541 acres, divided into the Canyons of the Escalante and Kaiparowits Horizon units. articles.title: Miliband says Britain won't tolerate threats on our soil, as Iran ambassador summoned
articles.summary: The prime minister says Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard "almost certainly" directed the RAF Fairford incident.
articles.body:
The foreign secretary has summoned the Iranian ambassador to make clear that "Britain will not tolerate threats on our soil" following last month's incident at RAF Fairford.

Ed Miliband said attempts by Iran to undermine the UK's security "through its criminal networks, proxy groups and state-backed malign activity is unacceptable".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told MPs the incident in Gloucestershire was "almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard", while the home secretary said the likely coordinator was a "known individual based in Iran".

Iran's ambassador to the UK, Seyed Ali Mousavi, said Tehran was not involved and was willing to cooperate with British authorities.

The Foreign Office has also sanctioned two Iranians, including the head of the regime's counterespionage operations - with both men subjected to travel bans and asset freezes.

Burnham also indicated Iran could be hit with further sanctions over its suspected role.

It comes as the UK and 28 other countries - including the US, Canada, Australia, France and Germany - issued a joint statement condemning "in the strongest terms" violent attacks by Iran.

The statement accuses Tehran of carrying out "lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities" and also recognises the UK's attribution of Iranian involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford.

A huge police operation began after officers were alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the base in the early hours of 27 September.

Dozens of homes were evacuated in the nearby village of Whelford and a large cordon was put in place around the site.

So far, a total of seven men - all in their 20s - have been arrested and later bailed in connection with the incident. No one has been charged.

Last week, Downing Street insisted the airbase was safe after the US withdrew all of its bombers – about a dozen B-1s from the base – back to their home stations on American soil.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

RAF Fairford, in the Cotswolds, has been used as a forward operating location by the US air force for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved an American request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

A US state department spokesman confirmed that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had a call with Miliband on Monday where they discussed "holding Iran to account for its actions and of continued collaboration to secure US assets in the United Kingdom".

articles.title: France school shooting: Police detain pupil after two injured
articles.summary: Officials say a staff member disarmed the suspect, who hid a hunting shotgun in a guitar case, before police arrived.
articles.body:
Police have detained a 14-year-old student suspected of shooting and wounding his middle school principal and teacher with a hunting rifle he hid in his guitar case, according to local officials.

Children ran for cover at Joseph Lakanal Middle School in Aubagne on Monday after the suspect fired multiple shots. The student fired once or twice on the first floor of the school, injuring the principal and teacher in the legs before he continued to the second floor and opened fire again, twice, Marseille Public Prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said in a statement.

A staff member disarmed the teen before police arrived and took him into custody, Mayor Jean-Pierre Squillari told reporters.

A third person was grazed in the shooting in the southern town near Marseille, while the headmaster and teacher were not in critical condition after being hit with ammunition used in 12-gauge shotguns, police said.

One student told Reuters that her maths teacher had played down the bang of the first gunshot blast as noise from nearby construction. A subsequent blast was followed by an alarm and classes emptied into the corridors.

“We were panicking; we ran,” the student said. “There were two ways out: one passage to the sports hall and one passage to go outside. Survival instinct took over, and I ran towards the outside.”

France’s Education Minister Edouard Geffray took to X to comment on the event and wrote, “This unacceptable act is yet further evidence of the rise of unchecked violence in our society, against which we must all take a stand.”

Gun violence perpetrated by pupils in schools is rare in France. In 2017, a 16-year-old student armed with a rifle, pistols and a small grenade opened fire at a high school in southern France, and wounded three students and the principal.

The prime minister’s office said the interior and education ministers were heading to the scene.

There was no immediate information to suggest that the shooting was in any way connected to protests by high school pupils demanding better-resourced schools that have been shaking France for several weeks.

articles.title: In Kenya, engineers added blue-gum wood ash to weak road-base soil; the mix achieved a 348% bearing score, over twice the 160% design requirement
articles.summary: Researchers in Kenya have successfully utilized blue gum wood ash to enhance weak road-base soil, achieving an impressive California bearing ratio (CBR) of 348%, significantly surpassing the standard design requirement of 160%. This innovative method could revolutionize road construction in Kenya, providing a more sustainable material option.
articles.body: Weak soil can make road construction more difficult, so engineers often use cement to strengthen road-base material. In a 2021 laboratory study, Blaise Dabou, Christopher Kanali and Zachary Abiero-Gariy investigated whether ash from blue gum trees (Eucalyptus globulus) could replace part of the cement used to stabilize lateritic soil. The researchers reported a peak soaked California Bearing Ratio (CBR) of 348% for a mixture containing 4% cement and 2% blue-gum wood ash by weight of soil. The result exceeded the 160% road-base benchmark cited from Kenya’s Road Design Manual.How wood ashes were usedLateritic soil develops in warm regions after extended weathering and is generally rich in iron and aluminium oxides, which give it a reddish or brown colour. Its engineering qualities exhibit significant location-dependent variation. Some lateritic soils are suitable for use in road building, whereas some need to be treated to provide the strength required for a pavement base. The researchers first tested the soil with Portland cement at levels ranging from 0% to 12% by weight of soil. They determined the California bearing ratio and unconfined compressive strength to select a cement-only mix that would be appropriate for subsequent testing.The mixture containing 6% cement recorded an unconfined compressive strength of 2.88 megapascals after seven days of curing. The researchers then wondered whether they might substitute some of the cement with blue gum wood ash while still making the material work as a road base.In the investigation on lateritic soil stabilised with cement and blue gum wood ash, the levels of replacement utilising the ash were investigated in incremental values. The optimum CBR was obtained at 2% blue gum wood ash. For the best effect, the ash replaced some of the original cement in the mix and was not the only stabilising material.The significance of the 348% resultThe soaking CBR of the combination with 4% cement and 2% blue gum wood ash was 348%. The unconfined compressive strength value after 7 days of curing was reported to be 2.99 megapascals. The CBR value of the cement- or lime-improved foundation material from Kenya’s Road Design Manual was compared with the benchmark of 160%.The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) test measures a soil or pavement material’s resistance to penetration relative to a standard crushed-rock reference material. Results are conventionally expressed as percentages, and values can exceed 100%. Therefore, the reported CBR of 348% is a penetration-resistance ratio, not a claim that the soil is 348% as strong or that a road built with it would last more than twice as long. This information enables road engineers to evaluate whether a material can resist the stresses anticipated in a pavement layer. The test must be read in conjunction with the curing conditions, moisture, soil properties and other strength values.The Ministry of Roads and Transport in Kenya has a manual on materials and pavement design that provides guidance on the use of soil classifications and material testing for constructing road structures. Such parameters are important since a laboratory value is only of practical importance if the test technique and material type are compatible with the specifications of the pavement which is intended to be built.Why the ash could helpWood ash is a mineral compound. The chemical composition is dependent on the tree type, burning circumstances of the wood, and the collection and treatment of the ash. When coupled with cement and soil, adequate ash particles and chemical elements can impact the compacted structure and the processes that occur during curing.The researchers found that a mix containing 4% cement and 2% wood ash achieved a seven-day compressive strength of 2.99 MPa, slightly higher than the 2.88 MPa recorded for the 6% cement-only mix. The combined mixture retained the same total additive content by weight of soil while replacing two percentage points of cement with wood ash. Before it could be used in a road project, engineers would have to examine its chemistry, particle size and consistency. Also, the soil itself has to be tested, because the same stabiliser can give different outcomes in different ground conditions.Limits of the lab resultsThe experiment was conducted on prepared soil samples under controlled settings. Moisture changes, traffic loading, drainage conditions, and quality of construction would affect field pavement. In the best-performing mixture, cement was still an essential part of the stabilising mechanism. articles.title: In 2018, UC San Diego tested a campus road made with recycled plastic in its asphalt mix, highlighting the promise and uncertainty of plastic-modified pavement
articles.summary: Explore how UC San Diego is pioneering the use of recycled plastic in road construction, reducing waste while enhancing pavement durability in a real-world traffic setting.
articles.body: Road surfaces rely on bitumen, a petroleum-derived binder that holds the mineral aggregates in asphalt together. In 2018, the University of California San Diego tested a different approach on a section of campus roadway, using recycled plastic materials in place of petroleum-based bitumen. The project simultaneously addressed the growing volume of discarded plastic and the ongoing need to maintain roads. MacRebur, instead of treating plastic as just a material to be disposed of or recycled, developed a process for blending it into asphalt mixtures. As per the university’s October 2018 news report, Gary Oshima, a construction commodity manager at UC San Diego, discovered the technology through a Facebook post featuring a TED Talk by MacRebur co-founder and chief executive Toby McCartney. This led Oshima to contact the company, which found a receptive response in their desire to make their debut in America.The methods for blending recycled plastic into asphalt Asphalt pavement typically combines mineral aggregates with a petroleum-derived binder called bitumen, which glues the particles together. Recycled plastic can be added using two primary methods: the dry process and the wet process, with each method differing in how the plastic interacts with the other materials. In the dry process, shredded or ground plastic is added directly to the mixture, and it serves either as a partial replacement for aggregate or as a modifier, whereas in the wet process, before it is combined with the aggregate, the plastic is blended into the asphalt binder. Ultimately, both methods strive to yield a modified binder with properties apt for the pavement application.According to the study, Use of Recycled Plastic in Asphalt and Concrete Pavement Applications, there are different technical challenges when these two methods are used. The National Centre for Asphalt Technology cautioned that the dry process could result in inconsistent mixture quality. Conversely, the wet process could separate the plastic from the binder because of chemical incompatibility and differences in viscosity and density.Understanding these distinctions matters because plastic waste is not a homogeneous material; different polymers such as polypropylene and polyethene terephthalate have distinct characteristics. Simply put, any one formulation that performs well with one type of polymer cannot be assumed to work the same with another, while other factors, such as particle size, dosage, mixing conditions, and the existing asphalt mixture, can also affect the result.What later research found Studies conducted in several countries have reported improvements, particularly in asphalt properties after recycled plastic was introduced. A 2020 Australian laboratory study, published two years after the campus test, found that recycled-plastic products led to an increase in binder resistance to flow and elasticity. The performance of the binder increased by three to four levels, and the resulting mixtures became stiffer and more deformation-resistant. However, the study did not find any notable improvements in terms of crack resistance or resistance to moisture damage.A review by Mashaan and colleagues in 2019, a year after the campus test, discussed studies and affirmed that the amount of plastic used also mattered, recommending different proportions of waste high-density polyethene and polyethene terephthalate for particular asphalt applications. However, those recommendations were in relation to the formulations examined; they do not establish a universal optimum for plastic-modified roads. The California Department of Transportation’s review also exhibited a shortage of domestic research and long-term field evidence. Although laboratory experiments and pilot installations opened up avenues for further investigation, at the time they could not determine the behaviour of plastic-modified pavement over many years of traffic, weather exposure and maintenance. The UC San Diego road has now carried traffic for eight years, yet no public condition data has surfaced, so its long-term performance remains unverified.Furthermore, environmental questions remain pertinent to that assessment, as researchers and officials have raised concerns about the potential for leaching, worker exposure during production and the difficulty of recycling plastic-containing asphalt at the end of its service life. Incorporating waste into pavement does not, by itself, demonstrate a net environmental benefit.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: UK PM Andy Burnham vows to renegotiate post-Brexit trade deal with EU
articles.summary: PM Burnham confirms talks in Brussels next month, insisting the British public will be ‘the boss’ of the reset.
articles.body:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to push for closer relations with the European Union, confirming he will attend a bilateral summit in Brussels next month.

Addressing parliament on Monday, Burnham said parts of the trade deal agreed with the EU after the UK voted to leave in 2016 would be renegotiated.

Burnham said that the British public would be “the boss” at every stage of renegotiating Britain’s relationship with the EU and that he wanted “serious dialogue” about long-term ties.

He told members of parliament that his focus at the summit would be boosting growth in the economy and controlling illegal immigration.

Among the topics of discussion at November’s summit are cutting bureaucracy for British food exports and emissions trading, as well as a “new youth experience scheme” and deeper cooperation on immigration.

The prime minister, who came into office in July, said the agreements could reverse some of the “damage” done to the post-Brexit British economy.

He told MPs that Britain needed to “ take a calm, clear-eyed look at the world as it is today”.

“Sticking to the status quo is not good enough,” he said, adding that “public opinion currently supports a pragmatic approach like the one I am suggesting”.

After his address, the leader of the opposition, Kemi Badenoch , said Burnham would be unable to secure a better deal as the EU was ” tough negotiators” and warned that he had already “shown his hand”.

In an interview released on Sunday, Burnham said it was “clear” that Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum and warned that French and German voters faced the same threat.

His comments marked the first time that a UK Prime Minister acknowledged Russian interference in the referendum, but did not provide evidence to support the claim.

articles.summary: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton listed her 2016 loss alongside 9/11 and COVID as hard times while addressing disillusioned Democrats.
articles.body: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton included her 2016 election loss on a list of hard times over the years in the U.S. during an event for Nebraska Democrats on Saturday, answering a question about how the Democratic base is feeling disillusioned about their vote. "And you could kind of understand that, for people who feel like they've had a series of hard times. If you look back on the last 25 years in our country, I was a senator from New York on 9/11. That was a trauma. The terrible financial crisis of 2008 was horrific for people. We had an election in 2016 that, you know, raised a lot of questions that we're still trying to find answers for about what, what kind of really went on, and then we had COVID," she told the crowd of Democrats. She continued, "So if you're somebody who is saying, does it really matter that I vote because I'm not sure I matter to the people that I'm asked to vote for? What we have to do is demonstrate as clearly as possible and then repeat over and over again, you do matter, and we're going to do everything we can to try to help you have the life you deserve to have." articles.title: On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged
articles.summary: Yemen's entrenched civil war is now impossible to ignore. But in operating rooms in its port city of Aden, geopolitics feels remote.
articles.body:
It was a journey at high speed through the desert - in a pick-up truck with armed fighters in the back. We were travelling with Yemen's pro-government forces, catching glimpses of the Arabian Sea, and forbidding mountain peaks in the distance. Houthi rebels were dislodged from here just days ago, we were told.

When you are battling over expanses of empty desert, progress can be hard to see. But these soldiers, in Shaab-al-Jinn in Lahj governorate, showed us new sandbagged defences - new lines in the sand.

"There was heavy fighting," said Tawfiq Al Haboun, a bearded commander in camouflage uniform.

"They have snipers, artillery and ballistic missile launchers."

Here in the far corners of the Middle East, a war is being waged with global implications.

Yemen's entrenched civil war is now impossible to ignore. It's part of a wider conflict, stretching from Tehran to Riyadh, where missiles slammed into the international airport this weekend . Yemen's Houthi fighters – already a threat to global shipping – are an increasing threat to Saudi Arabia. And they provide leverage for their backers in Iran, Saudi's regional rival.

Tawfiq Al Haboun pointed to shards of fibre glass and bits of metal at his feet – part of a downed Houthi drone that he said was carrying C4 explosives.

Commander Al Haboun is from the Southern Forces, part of the loose – very loose – alliance of groups fighting for Yemen's government, which is internationally recognised, and backed by Saudi Arabia and its air strikes.

The Houthis swept into the capital, Sanaa, in 2014, ousting the government. A year later a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened, trying to dislodge the Houthis. Despite years of devastating air strikes, that hasn't worked.

The commander tells us about 500 Houthi fighters remain on high ground overlooking a strategic maritime corridor – Bab al-Mandab – connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

The narrow waterway, which is crucial for oil exports, was just out of sight on our trip.

The Houthis seized the area after a lightning advance in September. The commander claims pro-government forces have wrested back about 85% (the Houthis have denied losing territory in other areas but not here, as far as our local sources know).

Until they regain complete control, there will be pressure on global oil supplies and on prices.

We heard later that there were heavy clashes the day of our visit. Five military vehicles apparently hit improvised explosive devices planted by the Houthis. It's unclear how many fighters were killed or injured.

As jitters run through international energy markets, hunger menaces weary Yemenis forced to flee this latest spasm of violence.

Around 200,000 have been driven from their homes since the start of this escalation at the beginning of September, according to the International Organization for Migration - all this in the Arab world's poorest country.

As we left the area, we saw a tableau of suffering with families dotted around seeking shelter under scrawny trees. Among one group of women and children we met Aisha, gaunt and elderly and sitting on the ground.

She fled in fear from her home in the Kahboob mountains – an area which has been hit by Houthi drone strikes.

"We have been here for 30 days," she told me.

"I have no animals, no money, no water, no food, not even a blanket... we had to run, with just the clothes on our backs."

At the weekend it was Saudi civilians at the international airport in Riyadh who were doing the running. The Houthi attack - the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade - sent shockwaves around the region and punctured the kingdom's sense of security.

But in operating rooms in Yemen's port city of Aden, geopolitics feels remote. Hospitals are overstretched and doctors are working night and day to treat wounded government fighters coming from the front lines.

We visited one military hospital where 51 casualties arrived in a single day – many with gunshot wounds, and several needing amputations.

In a crowded ward, a Houthi fighter lay alongside fighters from the other side. Doctors tell us they make no distinctions.

"I don't care where he comes from, his background or his religion. He is a human being so I should treat him as a human being, "said Dr Bassam Hazar.

Even if the war ends, some will never leave it behind. One man was sitting silently on his bed, a white bandage wrapped around the stump of his left arm, and staples running along his crown.

Others have not lost their fighting spirit, like Ahmed Ali Mahmoud who is smiling and animated, despite multiple fractures.

"I am not waiting to be fully recovered," he tells us.

"I just want to be able to stand. I think it is a religious duty and a national duty [to go back to fight]. The Houthis have destroyed the country. With victory I won't even feel these fractures."

In the next ward lies 12-year-old Ali, a brown-haired boy, who is just one year older than Yemen's civil war. Ali was injured by a drone as he walked down the street and is facing a complicated surgery.

"There is shrapnel near his spine," says Dr Amr Reyadh Assaqaf, standing by his bedside.

"The operation won't be easy, but God willing our staff will be able to handle it."

"At first he was depressed," he says, "but we gave him toys to play with and his mood is gradually lifting."

A truce in 2022 brought a few years of relative calm. But now the Houthis are a stronger enemy, as they have proven at the weekend. They already control most of Yemen's population. If there is a new attempt at mediation – and there is some speculation about this - they may drive a hard bargain.

Back at the hospital, as he prepares for the next wave of casualties, Dr Bassam Hazar hopes for change but doesn't expect it soon.

"Maybe war is good for news," he says, "but it's horrible [for people].

"Sons are losing their fathers, and mothers losing their sons. We need peace."

articles.summary: 31-year-old Ankur Patel, an Indian-origin Chicago man, killed his estranged wife, who left him and started dating another man.
articles.body: 31-year-old Ankur Patel, an Indian-origin Chicago man, killed his estranged wife, who left him and started dating another man. The incident took place in August when Patel lured his wife across the country on the pretext of allowing her to meet their five-year-old daughter. The woman's name was not released. According to reports, the woman left Patel in May and began dating one of their former colleagues.Out of family pressure, the woman gave Patel another chance and briefly moved back with him in Wisconsin. But she moved out shortly thereafter, allowing their daughter to remain with Patel. According to prosecutors, Patel proceeded to make threats over the phone to kill both the woman and the man she started dating after their breakup. He also stopped allowing the woman to speak with their daughter.Two weeks before the premeditated murder took place, Patel moved in with relatives in Chicago and sent his daughter to live with his parents in India. But he did not tell this to his estranged wife and instead invited her to meet the daughter. The woman had moved to Louisiana with the new man she had been seeing and she, along with the new boyfriend, drove to Chicago to get the child.Patel was seen purchasing a small folding knife on the surveillance cameras of a store. In the video, he was seen making stabbing and slicing motions with the knife. Then he went to the apartment where he asked his wife to come.Assistant State’s Attorney Mike Pekara said Patel's exchange with the woman was also recorded in surveillance footage. They initially argued as Patel expressed his desire to reunite. Patel allegedly recorded portions of the argument on his phone, but no physical violence was seen. At some point afterward, Pekara said, Patel brandished the knife and stabbed the woman in the neck. An autopsy later found that she had also suffered multiple defensive wounds, including a deep laceration to her left arm.The new boyfriend was outside the building and he repeatedly messaged the woman. Then he called 911 and explained the situation to them. Chicago Police Department tried to contact both the woman and Patel but could not reach either of them. Officers came to the site but they had to leave as the new boyfriend id not know which apartment the woman had entered.The same night, Patel made a plan with his friends, but he did not turn up. He checked into a nearby hotel where he disposed of the knife. He visited a Target store where he used his debit card to buy new shoes and clothes.The next day, he returned to the airport and purchased a ticket to India but the Department of Homeland Security had already been alerted and he was arrested. articles.title: Andy Burnham to push for new post-Brexit deals at EU summit
articles.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the prime minister was "unpicking" the deal the UK signed with the EU.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told MPs he will push for new post-Brexit deals with the EU at a summit next month.

He said "deeper cooperation" on some key issues - including youth mobility, food and drink, and energy - would help drive economic growth in the UK.

In a statement to MPs, Burnham also warned the EU's Made In Europe plans posed "a risk to UK manufacturing" and said he was in talks to get "an arrangement" that worked for the UK. The EU proposals aim to protect EU industry from Chinese competitors but could impact British industry and supply chains.

But Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the prime minister was "unpicking" the deal the UK signed with the EU.

Although he said he was keen to negotiate a closer relationship with the EU, Burnham made clear Labour's manifesto commitments not to return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement, would stay in place until the next election.

Burnham said the "immediate priority" was securing a successful outcome at the November summit, adding: "I believe we should then set up a serious dialogue about the different options for our relationship in the long term.

"At every stage, the British public will be the boss, and I am clear that public opinion currently supports a pragmatic approach like the one I am suggesting."

While the prime minister has committed to the current Labour manifesto's red lines about Brexit, in interviews after Labour conference, he did not rule out a new manifesto, which could include re-joining the EU.

It is increasingly clear that economic growth, and cooperation on illegal immigration, are going to be at the centre of No 10's arguments when it comes to selling a closer relationship both at - and beyond - next month's summit.

The Brexit withdrawal agreement in 2020 agreed the UK's "divorce bill" payments to the EU, and allowed the rules and regulations in the UK to start to diverge from those in the EU, which was necessary in order to negotiate trade deal with other countries .

But the divergence in food standards caused problems for UK food exports to its largest market, a problem that Sir Keir Starmer started to try to fix by renegotiating some common rules to reduce red tape.

In May 2025, this resulted in a post-Brexit deal agreeing continued access to UK waters for EU fishing boats until 2038, in return for a deal to reduce checks on food exports to the EU, which meant the UK was able to sell raw burgers and sausages back into the EU for the first time since Brexit.

The summit next month will see a series of deals with the EU on the table, Burnham told MPs, including food and drink, energy trading, and coordinating on immigration.

Burnham claimed these agreements could add the equivalent of £10bn per year to the economy by 2040, arguing that it would be a "dereliction of duty" to turn away from the chance to cut bureaucracy.

"At present entire truckloads of plants or fresh produce can be destroyed because of a single missing stamp or a minor paperwork delay," he said.

"Fresh meat and fish spoil while waiting in trucks, and tonnes of exports have to be written off. Our largest food export, Scottish salmon, faces a 100% rate of document checks at the border, costing us around £100m in lost exports.

"British burgers and other fresh meat products cannot be sold in the EU, seed potatoes from Scotland and shellfish from Wales are banned - this is having a real impact on businesses and the agreement on the table could reverse some of that damage."

The prime minister said a fresh agreement at the EU summit would also "ease the pressure on prices in the supermarket".

He said securing an energy deal, involving emissions trading, could "lower energy costs for households and businesses alike", adding this could cut wholesale energy costs by 20% in Northern Ireland.

Burnham said he also hoped to rebuild links with EU police and security agencies to boost information-sharing and help tackle smuggling gangs.

And he said being open about a new relationship with the EU was necessary to get a good deal on all these things: "If we are serious about promoting growth, controlling immigration, upholding our values and security, it is a conversation we must have.

"Sticking with the status quo is not good enough for Britain."

PM believes Brexit vote was legitimate despite Russia interference claims, No 10 says

Ten years on, Brexit's economic impact is becoming clearer

Who are the winners and losers from the UK-EU agreement?

The Conservative leader criticised the prime minister for "unpicking the deal this country signed with the EU a decade after the referendum".

Badenoch added Burnham would not get a better deal than the one secured by the Conservatives, accusing him of giving the game away ahead of the summit.

"His exact words earlier this year were, 'the last thing we should do right now is re-run those arguments' and yet here he is unpicking the deal this country signed with the EU a decade after the referendum," she said.

"He is not going to get a better deal. The EU are tough negotiators, and it's not just that the EU are tough negotiators, he has already revealed his entire negotiating hand.

"He has just blurted out everything he wants in this statement and I will tell him now, as a former trade secretary, this is not how you conduct negotiations."

Mocking the previous negotiations, Burnham said: "She says that, oh, I've revealed what I want to do and this isn't any way to negotiate it - because the Tories were so good, weren't they, at negotiating deals with our partners?"

Conservative Nigel Huddleston pointed out that post-Brexit trade deals with countries like the US and India meant a new EU deal would not be straightforward.

He said: "As a former trade minister can I also advise the PM, because his officials and minsters clearly have not, that actually it may not be as easy after all, because of clauses in some of the 70-something other trade deals that we did with other countries, to unwind all the things he would like to do."

However, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey welcomed Burnham's recognition of the "damage" of Brexit and called on him to go further, dropping Labour's red lines and opening negotiations on joining the EU single market and customs union.

articles.title: Llanfairfechan boy died after being hit by van while playing on bike
articles.summary: Harrison Jones suffered fatal head injuries after falling into the road, an inquest heard.
articles.body:
A six-year-old boy died after falling into the road and being hit by a van while playing on his bike, an inquest has heard.

Harrison Jones had been playing with a friend when he fell into the road outside his home in Llanfairfechan at about 17:30 BST on 1 October.

Denbighshire Coroner's Court heard he was struck by a passing Ford Transit tipper van.

A post-mortem examination found Harrison died from severe head injuries.

John Gittins, senior coroner for north Wales east and central, said the death required further investigation and adjourned the inquest.

In a tribute on a fundraising page launched to support his family, Harrison was described as a "cheeky chappy, full of character with a personality that could light up a room", and who had been "loved more deeply than words could ever express".

The GoFundMe fundraiser was launched by Kate Jones to help cover Harrison's funeral and memorial costs, as well as household bills and essential expenses while his parents take time away from work to grieve.

"There are no words that can truly describe the heartbreak and devastation his parents, sisters and our whole family are experiencing," Jones said on the fundraiser page.
