articles.title: For nearly 100 years, a Montana dam held back 6.6 million cubic yards of contaminated mining sediment; its removal helped reconnect two rivers and restore the landscape
articles.summary: For decades, the meeting point of the Clark Fork and Blackfoot rivers in western Montana lay behind a dam that held back more than water.
articles.body: For decades, the meeting point of the Clark Fork and Blackfoot rivers in western Montana lay behind a dam that held back more than water. Sediment carried downstream from copper mining around Butte had accumulated in the reservoir, leaving a legacy of contamination that reached beyond the river itself. Flooding and ice jams could stir the material up again, while arsenic from the mining waste affected nearby drinking water wells. By the time plans to remove the dam gained support, the problem had been building for almost a century. Its eventual removal changed the landscape at the confluence, allowing the rivers to reconnect and opening a new chapter in the area's restoration.How a 1908 flood spread toxic mining waste into Montana’s riversMilltown Dam stood near Missoula, where the Clark Fork meets the Blackfoot River, roughly eight miles upstream of the city. Built in the early 20th century, it created a reservoir that gradually filled with sediment washed down from mining operations in the Butte area. The consequences became especially apparent after a major flood in 1908 carried large quantities of mine waste into the river system.Over the years, contaminated material settled behind the dam. The reservoir eventually held an estimated 6.6 million cubic yards of sediment, according to the Clark Fork Coalition. That accumulation was not simply an environmental concern confined to the riverbed. Arsenic contamination reached local groundwater wells, and subsequent floods and ice jams could disturb polluted deposits, exposing aquatic habitats to further damage.How public pressure helped shape the Milltown Dam clean-up planThe Clark Fork Coalition, a conservation organisation working to protect the river system, spent years pressing for a more comprehensive response. One important step came in 1986, when the area was listed as a federal Superfund site, bringing it within a programme designed to address serious pollution requiring long-term remediation.Removing the dam was initially regarded by some as an unrealistic solution. Keeping the structure in place, however, would have left the reservoir and its contaminated sediment as continuing problems. The Coalition helped build public support for taking it down, working alongside residents and other groups concerned about water quality and the health of the river.The US Environmental Protection Agency ultimately endorsed dam removal as the preferred clean-up approach in 2003. The decision followed more than 10,000 public comments from people in western Montana supporting a full clean-up and the removal of the structure.The environmental restoration effort behind Milltown Dam’s removalThe polluted material accumulated in its reservoir had to be addressed as part of a wider remediation and restoration programme, rather than simply being left behind as the river changed course. The reservoir had contained millions of cubic yards of sediment, and managing that material was central to reducing the risks to people and wildlife. The work also required the river corridor to be restored so that the site could function as a floodplain again. Public agencies led the remediation and redevelopment process, with the Clark Fork Coalition contributing advice and representing community interests in decisions about the clean-up.Reportedly, the dam's removal was completed in 2008. With the obstruction gone and the restoration work under way, the confluence began to regain its role as a meeting point between two connected waterways, rather than a landscape shaped by a century of impounded water and contaminated deposits.Fish can move through the restored river confluenceWithout the dam separating the waterways, fish gained a more open route through the confluence of the Clark Fork and Blackfoot rivers. This matters for native trout, which rely on connected stretches of cold, clean water to reach suitable habitats and move through the river system.Restoring passage does not, by itself, guarantee that every fish population will recover. Water temperature, habitat quality and other environmental pressures still influence the health of a river. But removing a barrier can eliminate one obstacle to movement, allowing fish to use reaches that were previously difficult or impossible to access.The restored floodplain also gives the river corridor a different relationship with surrounding land. Rather than being confined by the former reservoir and dam, the area can accommodate natural river processes more readily.A former Superfund site becomes a place for public useThe area around the old dam has also taken on a new purpose. The restored confluence is part of Milltown State Park, which provides public access to a landscape once associated with industrial pollution and the hazards posed by contaminated sediment.Plans for the park have included walking trails, fishing access and picnic facilities, giving residents and visitors opportunities to spend time beside the rivers. The site offers space for activities such as angling, boating and birdwatching, while allowing people to see the results of the restoration at close quarters. Land that required extensive environmental intervention has become a public recreation area, with the rivers themselves once again central to the landscape. The park also gives the community a way to engage with the history of mining pollution and the lengthy process required to address it.What Milltown's restoration means for the Clark ForkThe removal of Milltown Dam addressed a local problem, but its significance extends across the connected river system. The Clark Fork carries water through a region affected by generations of mining, and pollution in one stretch can have consequences for communities and habitats further downstream. Reconnecting the rivers and dealing with the contaminated reservoir removed a longstanding source of risk at an important junction.The work was not a single engineering intervention followed by an instant return to pristine conditions. It depended on years of advocacy, public involvement, regulatory decisions, sediment management and the restoration of the land around the former reservoir. Monitoring and wider watershed clean-up remain important to the long-term health of the rivers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Crew searching for Amelia Earhart plane lands at remote island infested with carnivorous crabs
articles.summary: Researchers will sleep on their ship to avoid giant crabs that can lift heavy weights, split open coconuts, and may have played a role in Earhart's demise.
articles.body:
A team of researchers have arrived at a remote island to inspect possible plane wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart, who vanished in 1937 while flying around the world.

The group from the Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University arrived at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean on Monday.

The search team's work, expected to take five days, could be hampered by giant land-dwelling crabs, as well as the El Niño climate phenomenon which is now the strongest ever recorded .

Coconut crabs, also known as Robber crabs, emerge at night to hunt for small mammals and seabirds, and will force the search crew to spend nights on their ship for their own safety.

The disappearance of Earhart, an American aviation pioneer who was attempting to circumnavigate the globe with navigator Fred Noonan, has spawned decades of speculation.

Researchers will work to locate what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020.

Some believe it to be the wreckage of her plane, but others have expressed scepticism that it is an aircraft at all, with one theory suggesting it is a collapsed tree.

This is the first authorised trip to Nikumaroro Island in seven years, and the first visit to the Taraia Peninsula in more than 15, according to Purdue.

The ship, the Marin Mainiku, on Monday arrived at the western side of the island, part of the nation of Kiribati, after a five-day voyage crossing 830-nautical-miles through the South Pacific.

"It is incredibly rewarding to be this close to completing our inspection of the Taraia Object and potentially solving, at long last, the outstanding mystery of the disappearance of Amelia Earhart and Fred Noonan more than 89 years ago," expedition leader Rick Pettigrew said in a blog post on Monday.

On Tuesday, the crew plans to navigate through a narrow gap "blasted" in the atoll's reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited - to prepare for landing.

The first day on the island will focus on "transporting equipment, clearing vegetation, and establishing staging operations", according to the post. One group of researchers will cut a trail through the jungle.

Work will then shift to searching for evidence, including magnetic metals, on the Taraia Peninsula on Wednesday.

Lastly, the researchers will use dredging equipment to move sediment for a visual inspection of the mystery object, which is believed to be located only 10 feet from the shore in as little as five feet of water (depending on the tides).

Weather and ocean conditions "will continue to be a factor", researchers say, and El Niño could limit daily access to shore. Michael Krivor, a marine archaeologist on the trip, said he is currently concerned about a weather pattern traveling from east to west that could interfere with "safe transit in and out of the blasted channels".

Another concern is the crabs, the largest land-dwelling invertebrates on the planet.

"The crew will sleep nightly aboard the Marin Mainiku for a number of reasons, one of which is the presence of coconut crabs, whose size and overnight activity make staying on the island impractical," the blog post says.

The crabs, which occupy atolls and desert islands throughout the South Pacific, can lift up to 28kg (62lbs), and are one of the only species that can crack open a coconut, although they also hunt for live prey like rats and birds.

With a leg span of up to one metre and a body weight of more than 4kg, they are also the world's largest land-dwelling crustacean and are able to climb trees.

In 2018, the International Group of Historical Aircraft Recovery used pig carcasses to demonstrate how the crabs were able to drag bodies to their burrows and strip the bones of flesh in less than two weeks.

Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her Electra twin-engine plane when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea, on 2 July 1937.

From there, she and Noonan planned to travel towards Hawaii, but the plane vanished without a trace as they tried to reach uninhabited Howland Island, near Nikumaroro, to refuel.

While there have been numerous theories about the disappearance, the official explanation is that the plane suffered communication problems and, as she and Noonan struggled to find the island, the plane ran out of fuel and crashed into the ocean.

articles.title: Poland says two Turks arrested over Russia-linked Starlink station fire
articles.summary: Warsaw says the 2 suspects held in Germany will face sabotage charges.
articles.body:
Two Turkish citizens have been detained in Germany over a fire at a Starlink station in central Poland that Warsaw has branded an act of sabotage carried out on Russia’s behalf.

Polish officials announced the arrests on Monday, one month after the fire, which they say was aimed at disrupting internet services, including for Ukraine’s military. The fire, in Masovia in Eastern Poland, engulfed the Starlink station’s power system and backup generator.

Polish Minister of Interior Marcin Kierwinski said the two men would face charges in Poland of carrying out sabotage on the instructions of a foreign intelligence agency. German police made the arrests on behalf of Polish services, according to Deutsche Welle. Polish officials did not say where or when in Germany the men were detained.

“We have no doubt that Russian services are behind this act of sabotage,” Special Services Minister Tomasz Siemoniak said in a news conference. “It is worth adding that Russian services are increasingly turning to individuals linked to the criminal underworld,” he said.

The case is the latest in a string of incidents that officials across the European Union deem to be part of a Russian campaign of sabotage and hybrid attacks aimed at eroding support for Ukraine.

The Russian embassy in Warsaw did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Moscow has previously dismissed similar accusations as baseless and the product of anti-Russian hysteria.

Ukraine’s military relies on tens of thousands of Starlink terminals for battlefield communications and occasional drone operations. Starlink founder Elon Musk activated the service over Ukraine in 2022, days after Russia’s full-scale invasion, following a plea from Kyiv. Poland has said it pays for Ukraine’s Starlink subscription.

Musk has since clashed with Ukrainian officials over his views on the war. This year, he also agreed to switch off thousands of Russian “grey-market” Starlink terminals in Ukraine, causing problems for Russian forces. Ukraine is now seeking to use the terminals for attacks on Russian territory.

articles.title: INDIA bloc files petition in SC on SIR voter deletions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc members, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, undertook their
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc members, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and joined by thousands of supporters, undertook their march to Supreme Court on Monday to file a joint petition seeking intense scrutiny into a host of issues - functioning of EC, preventing CEC Gyanesh Kumar from taking decisions "unilaterally", "arbitrary" deletion of voters during SIR, and the architecture governing use and deployment of EVMs.Rahul and other petitioners - Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer - sought suspension of SIR without questioning its legality, and, inclusion of eligible voters in rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.On CJI's refusal to meet the opposition delegation, Rahul said, "We respect CJI and SC. We are quite happy he has given us a path forward. To tell us we can file a petition is a path forward." The petition requested the court to set up a panel led by a retired SC judge, comprising technical experts and persons of eminence to "examine integrity of electoral-roll databases and SIR rollout".INDIA bloc seeks complete files, objections by ECs to SIR, access logs, meeting minutesThe petitioners also wanted the panel to ‘review processes, procedures, protocols and technical architecture governing EVMs’.They said, “The validity of SIR does not dispense with the requirement that each decision taken in its implementation must conform to Constitution, governing statutes and applicable rules.”The present plea is instituted in the larger public interest of safeguarding the constitutional right of every eligible citizen to vote, maintaining institutional independence and collective functioning of EC, and ensuring that the preparation and revision of poll rolls are carried out transparently, lawfully and in a manner that inspires public confidence in the democratic process, the opposition functionaries argued.Flagging alleged unlawful modification of Form 6, used for enrolment of new voters, the petitioners, through advocate Prasanna S, said, “Addition of an unauthorised condition to a statutory form may impose an unlawful burden upon eligible citizens seeking registration, particularly first-time voters, and may result in the exclusion of persons otherwise entitled to be enrolled.”The SC registry pointed out several defects in the petition, and the counsel said he will cure them in due course.The opposition members also objected to centralised and opaque functioning of ECINET and ERONET poll rolls database and the “large-scale exclusion of voters without adequate notice, hearing or an effective mechanism for restoration in case of wrongful or erroneous deletions”.Invoking fundamental rights of people under Articles 14, 19, 21 read with Article 324 (EC) of the Constitution, they sought a direction from SC to EC to produce in court “complete files, agendas, minutes, file noting and objections recorded by election commissioners in respect of each of the disputed decisions related to SIR, together with relevant ECINET and ERONET access logs and complete file recording on EC’s June 24, 2025 decision to commence SIR across the country”.Pending decision on the petition, they said EC must function as per the mandate of the Constitution in a democratic manner and ensure Form 6 conformed to Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.They wanted EC to “publish, booth-wise, the names of all electors deleted during the SIR, together with the reasons for each deletion and a breakdown of deletions by gender and age, and to provide an effective and functional mechanism for restoring the names of electors found eligible for inclusion in the poll rolls”.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
